_comment: Golden answer for DOP-005. Must score 1.0 under grader.mjs. Written from the fix that shipped in 586ec2f0 and the reasoning already recorded in server.js and scripts/test_site_hygiene.mjs.
culprit: The stored address is not the visitor: it is the loopback address of Render's in-instance reverse proxy. The app never set `trust proxy`, so Express derives `req.ip` from the socket peer, and the socket peer is always that proxy on ::1.
evidence: The page lines read ::1 on the admin dashboard on 2026-04-18 and on the landing page on 2026-10-11 — different surfaces, six months apart, identical value. The peer that got ::1 also pulled ten media range requests (about 40 MB inside 13 s) and POSTed track-visit; a health checker does not fetch ten videos and post analytics, so that peer was a browser belonging to a real person. In the tables every ip and source_ip row reads ::1 while the session ids differ and do not overlap in time, so separate visitors collapse into one address.
why_it_was_missed: Nothing errored and nothing looked malformed. The app wrote a well-formed address, and the address it wrote is loopback, which reads as local traffic rather than as a fault; every downstream column inherited it, so the analytics looked consistent instead of wrong. The only visible symptom was that everybody appeared to come from one place, which is a plausible-looking business fact rather than a technical error, so nobody opened the log.

fix.ordering: before express.json() parses the first body, and before the request logger reads req.ip

must_not: It must not be `true`. Trusting every hop means the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value is believed, and that value is client-supplied, so any visitor can spoof any address and the analytics become forgeable. The correct value is the hop count of one, because there is exactly one proxy in front of the app.
does_not_fix: It does not identify the person behind a VPN, a corporate NAT or a shared mobile-carrier address — those still share one address, and that is correct behaviour. It also does not fix the favicon 404s or the 40 MB of media the landing page pulls. It only makes the stored address the visitor's instead of the proxy's; genuine local development traffic is ::1 and must keep reading that way.
